The last version that actually reached the registry is 0.46.0. Two different errors were reported over that period: - `npm error code ENEEDAUTH` (Rust workflow, runs 30166422548 / 30240588949) - `npm error code E404 / 404 Not Found - PUT https://registry.npmjs.org/meta-language` (JavaScript workflow, runs 30733403030 / 30735100706) Both have one root cause. `actions/setup-node` with `registry-url` unconditionally writes `//registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken=${N…KEN}` into `$NPM_CONFIG_USERCONFIG` and exports the placeholder `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN=XXX…XX` when no token is supplied. npm then considers itself authenticated, **never performs the OIDC exchange** required by trusted publishing, and the registry rejects the anonymous upload — as `404`, not `403`. With an empty token the same line yields `ENEEDAUTH` instead. The placeholder is visible in our own logs: every step of the failing publish job shows `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN: XXX…XX`, even though the workflow set no token at that commit. Upstream: [actions/setup-node#1440](https://github.com/actions/setup-node/issues/1440), [#1551](https://github.com/actions/setup-node/issues/1551), fixed by [PR #1558](https://github.com/actions/setup-node/pull/1558) — which shipped **only on the v7 line**; `@v6` (v6.5.0, what the floating tag resolves to) still contains the placeholder in its built bundle. Removing `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` from the workflow — what #177 did — was not enough, because the npmrc line is written regardless. ## Changes - **`js/scripts/prepare-npm-auth.mjs`** (new). Resolves the auth mode (`token` / `oidc` / `none`), strips the placeholder `_authToken` line so the OIDC handshake actually happens, removes the deprecated `always-auth` key npm 11 warns about, and exits non-zero with remediation instructions when no credential exists at all. - **`.github/workflows/js.yml`**. Runs the script between `setup-node` and `npm publish`, keeps an optional `NPM_TOKEN` bootstrap fallback, and adds a failure explainer so an `E404` names its real cause. - **Tests.** `js/tests/prepare-npm-auth.test.js` covers the behaviour, including a case that reproduces the bug. `js/tests/package-release.test.js` previously asserted `doesNotMatch(workflow, /NODE_AUTH_TOKEN/)` — it was locking in the broken configuration; it now asserts the intended state. - **Docs.** A troubleshooting section for this failure, and `NPM_TOKEN` added to the secrets table. - **Evidence.** All downloaded run logs, the best-practices document, the deep analysis, and the upstream report record under `dev/log/issues/191/pulls/192/`. ## Findings by category - **False positive:** the `E404` — the package exists and the version is new; the real fault is a skipped OIDC exchange. - **False negative:** a release could complete green with the npm package never published, and the test suite actively defended the broken configuration. The script now fails before `npm publish` when no credential is available. - **Warning:** the deprecated `always-auth` key, now removed in every mode. - **Error:** `E404` / `ENEEDAUTH`, addressed above. Compared both workflows against the three `link-foundation/*-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template` repositories and `hive-mind/docs/CI-CD-BEST-PRACTICES.md`. Least-privilege permissions, serialised writer concurrency with cancellable `check-*` read groups, `!cancelled()` conditions, per-job timeouts, `env:` indirection for untrusted inputs, and idempotent publish with post-verification were already conformant. The one gap was the npmrc sanitisation. ## Upstream The JS template's `scripts/sanitize-npm-userconfig.mjs` strips only `always-auth` and leaves the `_authToken` line, so every project generated from it inherits this bug. Reported with a reproducible example, a workaround, and a suggested code fix: link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template#120. The Rust and Python templates are unaffected — neither publishes to npm. ## Reproduction and verification The failing case is reproduced as a unit test (`OIDC runs unblock the npmrc that setup-node wrote`) using the exact npmrc `setup-node` writes; it fails without the fix and passes with it. Locally: `npm test` → 89 passing, `npm run check:parity` → clean, and the repository secretlint scan passes over the newly added logs. ## Note for the maintainer The code fix makes the OIDC attempt genuinely happen, but publishing also requires a trusted publisher registered for `meta-language` on npmjs.com pointing at `link-foundation/meta-language` with workflow file `.github/workflows/js.yml`. That is account-side configuration and cannot be done from a PR. Until it exists, set an `NPM_TOKEN` secret and the bootstrap path takes over; either way the job now reports exactly which one is missing instead of an `E404`.
